memory_candidates.content: When a script self-resolves its project root from BASH_SOURCE[0] (not CWD) and has no --state/--todo override flag (e.g. manage-topics.sh), the only correct multi-repo invocation is an absolute, fully-qualified path passed to `bash`. A chained `cd && script` also works but must be re-derived in every separate Bash tool call since shell cwd does not persist across invocations -- absolute paths avoid that failure mode entirely and should be the default; reserve chained cd for git only.

Static `@`-file-reference syntax in agent definitions cannot be parameterized by a runtime variable (e.g. target_root) -- it always resolves against the current session's own deployment. Any context-loading instruction that must read a runtime-resolved path (e.g. analyze-mode inventorying a foreign repo) must be rewritten as an explicit runtime `Read {variable}/...` instruction instead of `@`-syntax.
